public_body: Middleton Flint Library Board Of Trustees
overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating through a serial email chain among a quorum about board leadership; further-review allegations on dissemination, secret ballot, and incivility were not reviewed.

allegations.summary: Board members allegedly deliberated by email before a June meeting on reorganizing officers, including the chair race, outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, because a quorum of the Board communicated in a serial manner outside of a noticed meeting and discussed the leadership of the Board, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: On further review, complainant alleged the Board failed to disseminate the complaint to all members, which was not in the original complaint to the Board.
allegations.key_passage: We find that these allegations were not clearly raised in the original complaint and thus we do not review their merits.

allegations.summary: On further review, complainant alleged the Board voted by secret ballot during the reorganization; not raised in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We find that these allegations were not clearly raised in the original complaint and thus we do not review their merits.

allegations.summary: On further review, complainant alleged uncivil behavior by members during the meeting; not raised in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, an allegation of unprofessional conduct or incivility towards members of the Board does not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Publicly release the emails within 30 days of receipt of the determination, to the extent not already done.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
